name: Loaded Bristle 120
notes: An oil brush that keeps its comb through a turn: the tip follows the stroke direction, and the dual mask breaks the body up so a long stroke never reads as one flat ribbon. Flow over spacing sets the flank hardness — here it is high enough to square the edge off, which is what separates a loaded brush from a wash. Because that ratio saturates the mark at every pressure, pressure is bound to Transfer opacity as well: without it, a light stroke and a heavy one lay down the same ink and the brush feels dead.
